text: While the wind is busy rearranging every skyline on Earth, the oceans are quietly plotting something even worse.

Because the Earth normally spins, centrifugal force pushes ocean water outward toward the equator, creating a giant invisible bulge around the middle of the planet—almost thirteen miles thicker than at the poles.
The instant rotation hits zero, that outward push vanishes. First, every coastline on the planet gets slammed by mile-high megatsunamis as trillions of tons of water slosh violently eastward.

Then, gravity pulls all that equatorial water north and south toward the poles. Within minutes, two massive polar oceans begin swelling while a brand-new band of exposed, muddy seabed dries out around the equator.
So if you bought beachfront property near the tropics, good news: you now own a giant desert. Bad news: your inflatable pool float is currently headed for Antarctica.
